Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <3la7ut$d...@newsbf02.news.aol.com>, mal...@aol.com (Malkav) wrote:

> I have a question about the effects of Disarming Presence. Sure, all
> vampires that vote are tapped (though with sup. pres. YOURS aren't) but
> does that mean that already tapped vampires cannot vote? I've gotta know,
> this has caused violent arguments (a splintered skull here 'n' there)!
>
I don't remember when I read it on the net, (I think a mamber of my group
brought in a print out from a couple of weeks ago)but here is how our
group plays. The tapping of the vampire is a result of the vote, not a
cost of the vote. Therefore, if a vampire is tapped, it can vote with no
consequences. The kicker is that if your vampires are untapped, you risk
a weakened defense if you vote.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
mal...@aol.com (Malkav) writes:

>I have a question about the effects of Disarming Presence. Sure, all
>vampires that vote are tapped (though with sup. pres. YOURS aren't) but
>does that mean that already tapped vampires cannot vote?

This is a tough question, because the normal level implies tapped vampires
CAN vote, and the superior that they CAN'T. The DTR has said that it's
the first interpretation; tapped vampires can vote without penalty.
Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Design Team Ruling (11/9/94):

> The tapping is a side effect, not a cost, so tapped vampires can still vote.
